observations.text: SP met the block requirement, completing the departure from the flight area and the descent to the VFR entry point with the IP directing the descent check and the entry sequence. Altitude at the entry point was 400 feet high and airspeed 25 knots fast before the IP assumed the descent profile. Marginal performance for the Training Section - knowledge of the entry points and the approach procedures is expected to improve so that verbal prompting alone becomes sufficient.

SP, without the IP directing or executing any part of the procedure, departed the flight area as determined in the LAP and descended toward the VFR entry point after obtaining the required clearance. The required descent check was completed following the IP's verbal prompts, with deviations of 300 feet in altitude and 10 degrees on the entry heading recognized and corrected with delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP performed the required descent check and procedure without IP's intervention and navigated to the assigned VFR entry point after obtaining the required clearance. Minor errors in descent planning produced deviations of 200 feet in altitude and 15 knots in airspeed, recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP performed the required descent check and procedure accurately and promptly, descending prior to the entry point in a timely manner after obtaining the required clearance. The entry point and the approach procedure were identified without reference to the IP, and no adjacent flight area was violated. Deviations remained within 120 feet in altitude, 8 knots in airspeed and 4 degrees on the entry heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the descent and traffic pattern entry with exceptional accuracy, completing the required descent check and procedure well before the entry point and using the VOR and GPS to confirm position without prompting. Deviations were negligible, within 50 feet in altitude, 3 knots in airspeed and 2 degrees on the entry heading, and no adjacent flight area was approached. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized descent check flow, did not complete the required descent check and procedure before departing the flight area and did not descend prior to the entry point in a timely manner. Altitude at the VFR entry point was 500 feet high and airspeed 30 knots fast, with the result that the IP directed the profile and executed part of the entry sequence.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published procedure for the condition encountered, did not identify the assigned VFR entry point and did not use the VOR and GPS to orient in space and return to the airport. The descent was flown 450 feet above the entry altitude and 25 knots fast, with the result that the IP directed the recovery track and flew part of the pattern entry.

SP completed the descent and traffic pattern entry to the standard required for this block, performing the required descent check and reaching the VFR entry point after the IP's verbal prompts. Altitude deviation reached 300 feet and airspeed deviation 20 knots at the entry point, recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier initiation of the descent and independent recognition of the entry point are expected to improve.

SP performed the required descent check and procedure without IP's intervention and obtained the required clearance before descending toward the VFR entry point. Minor errors in the timing of the descent produced deviations of 180 feet in altitude and 12 knots in airspeed, recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP performed the required descent check and procedure accurately and promptly, navigating and descending prior to the entry point in a timely manner after obtaining the required clearance. The entry points and the approach procedures were known without reference to the IP, and no adjacent flight area was violated. Deviations remained within 130 feet in altitude, 7 knots in airspeed and 4 degrees on the entry heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the descent and traffic pattern entry with accuracy above the desired level, completing the required descent check early and cross-checking the VOR and GPS to confirm the entry point without prompting. Deviations were negligible, within 40 feet in altitude, 3 knots in airspeed and 1 degree on the entry heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a descent profile planned without reference to the distance remaining to the entry point, did not descend prior to the entry point and did not complete the required descent check and procedure. The A/C arrived at the VFR entry point 600 feet high and 30 knots fast, with the result that the IP directed the descent and executed part of the pattern entry.

SP, due to absorption in a cockpit indication that left the descent rate unmonitored, did not perform the required descent check and did not obtain the required clearance before descending toward the entry point. The A/C passed the entry altitude by 450 feet with airspeed 28 knots above the briefed value, with the result that the IP directed the level-off and flew part of the entry to the traffic pattern.

SP, due to late initiation of the descent from the flight area, did not navigate and descend prior to the entry point in a timely manner, and the required descent check was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts. Altitude at the VFR entry point was 300 feet high and airspeed 20 knots fast, recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to workload management that left the checklist unfinished before the descent, did not perform the required descent check and procedure and did not identify the assigned entry point without assistance. The entry was completed after the IP's verbal prompts, with the entry heading 10 degrees off and airspeed 20 knots fast, recognized and corrected with delay.

SP performed the descent and traffic pattern entry within the desired standards, obtaining the required clearance and completing the descent check without IP's intervention. Deviations of 190 feet in altitude and 14 knots in airspeed were twice recognized and corrected in a timely manner during the descent to the VFR entry point. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter control of the descent profile and of airspeed toward the entry point is expected to improve.

SP performed the required descent check and procedure accurately and promptly, descending prior to the entry point in a timely manner after obtaining the required clearance and demonstrating knowledge of the entry points and the approach procedures. No adjacent flight area was violated and no IP prompting was required. Deviations remained within 110 feet in altitude, 6 knots in airspeed and 3 degrees on the entry heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the departure from the flight area and the descent to the VFR entry point with exceptional accuracy, completing the required descent check ahead of the descent and using the VOR and GPS to confirm position without prompting. Deviations were negligible, within 50 feet in altitude, 4 knots in airspeed and 2 degrees on the entry heading, and the entry to the traffic pattern was flown as briefed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect computation of the descent point for the recovery track, did not descend prior to the entry point and did not complete the required descent check and procedure. The A/C reached the VFR entry point 550 feet high and 30 knots fast, with the result that the IP directed the profile and executed part of the pattern entry.

SP, due to lack of awareness of the aircraft's position relative to the area boundary, did not depart the flight area on the track determined in the LAP and entered the adjacent flight area during the descent. Airspeed reached 28 knots above the briefed value and the entry heading was 20 degrees off, with the result that the IP directed the turn back to the assigned entry point and flew part of the descent.

SP, due to a descent initiated without cross-checking the distance remaining to the VFR entry point, did not navigate and descend prior to the entry point in a timely manner, and the required descent check was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts. Deviations reached 300 feet in altitude and 20 knots in airspeed at the entry point, recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to loss of situational awareness of the aircraft's position in the pattern, did not identify the assigned VFR entry point and did not apply the corresponding approach procedure. The entry was completed after the IP's verbal prompts, with the entry heading 10 degrees off and altitude 300 feet high, recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to a descent rate set without adjustment for the tailwind component, did not maintain the planned descent profile toward the VFR entry point, although the descent check and the required clearance were completed as prescribed. Altitude at the entry point was 200 feet high and airspeed 15 knots fast, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on the recovery track, did not perform the required descent check in the prescribed sequence and delayed the descent toward the VFR entry point. The resulting deviations were 220 feet in altitude and 8 degrees on the entry heading, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention.

SP performed the required descent check and procedure accurately and promptly, descending prior to the entry point after obtaining the required clearance and without IP's intervention. Deviations remained within 140 feet in altitude and 9 knots in airspeed, twice reaching the limits of the desired standard during the descent. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency of the descent profile and of airspeed control toward the VFR entry point is expected to improve.

SP executed the departure from the flight area and the descent to the VFR entry point with exceptional accuracy, completing the required descent check well ahead of the descent and cross-checking the VOR and GPS to confirm the entry point without prompting. Deviations were negligible, within 40 feet in altitude, 3 knots in airspeed and 2 degrees on the entry heading, and no adjacent flight area was approached. Above end of block MIF achieved.
